candidates.evidence: Two Raman bands at 383.81 cm-1 (FWHM 2.03) and 403.29 cm-1 (FWHM 3.74), i.e. an E^1_2g-type / A1g-type pair with separation 19.48 cm-1 (calibration-independent). This pair is the MoS2 signature; the Si line at 520.91 cm-1 fits 'Si substrate' with +0.21 cm-1 offset vs the stated 520.7. No WS2 (E2g ~356 / A1g ~420) or MoSe2 (E2g ~286 / A1g ~243, reversed order) pattern is present. Layer number: separation 19.5 cm-1 is closest to the monolayer value in Lee et al. (arXiv:1005.2509, Fig. 2b; difference approx. 18.5-19 cm-1 at 1L, approx. 21-22 at 2L, approx. 25 for 4L-bulk), so 1L most likely with 2L as the main alternative.

The 1T phase would show J1/J2/J3 bands near 150/227/335 cm-1 and no E2g/A1g pair at 384/403. Nothing resolved above noise in the 150-350 cm-1 region, and the 383.8/403.3 pair is not 1T-like. Retained only for completeness.

hint_reasoning: No material hint was given. The identification is from the spectrum: the E2g/A1g pair at 383.8/403.3 cm-1 with separation 19.5 cm-1 points to 2H-MoS2. Layer number is one of 1L or 2L from the separation against literature; the spectrum alone (150-650 cm-1, no shear or breathing mode in range) cannot separate 1L from 2L with confidence.

peaks.source: Own fit (quadratic background + Lorentzian, scipy curve_fit), stat error 0.02 cm-1; assignment from Lee et al., arXiv:1005.2509 (ACS Nano 2010)

peaks.source: Own fit, stat error 0.05 cm-1; assignment from Lee et al., arXiv:1005.2509 (ACS Nano 2010)

artifacts.type: cosmic-ray spike (single sample point, not a Raman band)
noise-level features at 2-5 sigma (not reproducible, not reported as peaks; e.g. 630.5, 357.6, 291.5 cm-1)

citations: Lee, C. et al., Anomalous lattice vibrations of single- and few-layer MoS2, ACS Nano 2010, doi:10.1021/nn1003937, arXiv:1005.2509 (abstract: E^1_2g frequency decreases and A1g increases with thickness; Fig. 2b frequencies and difference vs layer number, read by eye)
Task statement: Si reference line at 520.7 cm-1
limits: Analysis done in the working folder only with my own Python code. I did not use the skill's scripts or its reference notes (materials notes, relations, artifacts list) because they live outside this folder; the Lee et al. thresholds were taken from the paper via the literature tool instead, read off a plot (approx. +/-0.5 cm-1).

Layer number: one spectrum cannot give it unambiguously. Separation 19.5 cm-1 sits between the monolayer (about 18.5-19) and bilayer (about 21-22) values in Lee et al. (SiO2/Si, 514 nm in that work as far as I know, not verified in the paper text here). The data window (150-650 cm-1) excludes the low-frequency shear and layer-breathing modes (about 20-40 cm-1), which are the decisive check between 1L and 2L. Recommend measuring below 50 cm-1 or a PL check.

Absolute positions: E2g 383.6 and A1g 403.1 (after Si offset correction) are a little low for a monolayer on SiO2 in Lee et al. (E2g about 384.3, A1g about 403 at 1L by eye). Laser (532 nm here), substrate and strain/doping can shift these by about 0.5-1 cm-1, so they are not used to set the layer number; only the separation is.

Weak features: 2LA(M) near 450-455 cm-1, LA(M) near 230 cm-1 and E^1_2g near 286 cm-1 are not resolved. The apparent 453.5 band is a single-point spike; the 230, 286, 357 and 630 cm-1 features are below 5 sigma and not reproducible under window changes, so I report none of them.

Background: a broad slope 2300-4000 cm-1 counts across 150-500 cm-1 is present but not interpreted (could be fluorescence or substrate). It does not affect the peak positions, which come from local fits with a quadratic background.
Noise sigma about 148 counts; no polarization or angle series, so no polarization class is assigned. Temperature 295 K assumed for all position comparisons (no temperature shift applied).

Si calibration: 520.91 vs 520.7 gives +0.21 cm-1 offset, applied only to the absolute positions in the text. The separation 19.48 cm-1 is unaffected by calibration. Stat errors are fit-only; calibration uncertainty is a few tenths of a cm-1.
